title: Europe Wildfires 2026: 3 Firefighters Killed, 254,000 Hectares Burned Across France, Spain and Italy
excerpt: Three firefighters dead, 10,000 evacuated overnight — Europe's wildfires have already burned 254,388 hectares in 2026, making it the second worst season in 20 years. What's fuelling the crisis?
content:
Three firefighters have died this week as wildfires tear through France, Spain, and Italy, forcing more than 10,000 people from their homes overnight.

The two French firefighters died on July 21 while battling a fire near Bordeaux-Mérignac airport in the Gironde department of southwestern France. In Sicily, a firefighter named Alessandro Marchi died after falling ill while fighting a fire near the town of San Cataldo. Italy's Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi confirmed the death.

In the Gironde, a fire near the Arcachon basin burned through more than 2,000 hectares in a single night, pushing more than 10,000 residents to evacuate. The Arcachon basin is one of France's most visited summer destinations — home to the Dune de Pilat and its oyster industry. A July evacuation during peak season has left local businesses counting losses alongside the damage.

In Spain's Guadalajara province, the La Mierla blaze consumed approximately 32,000 hectares — placing it among the largest single fires in Spanish recorded history. Thirty-four municipalities were evacuated. Five of those towns have since been given clearance to return after the fire entered a stabilization phase, though conditions across the broader region remain active.

In Sicily, around 6,000 firefighters, forest guards, and civil protection workers are battling dozens of fires across the island, supported by water-bombing aircraft. Temperatures on the ground topped 40°C. Wildfire smoke carrying fine particulate matter has affected air quality across parts of southern Europe, raising concerns for people with asthma and respiratory conditions.

This is not the first time the Bordeaux region has faced a crisis like this. In 2022, the Gironde department lost over 26,000 hectares in France's worst modern wildfire event, forcing more than 36,000 people to leave. That same region burning again in 2026 — just four years later — shows how short the recovery window has become.

According to the European Forest Fires Information System, wildfires have burned approximately 254,388 hectares across the EU in 2026. That already places this year as the second largest EU wildfire season in 20 years — with summer months still ahead. Over the same period in 2025, approximately 270,449 hectares had burned.

European Commissioner Hadja Lahbib has described wildfires as "a new reality" for Europe, noting that fires now start earlier, burn for longer, and reach areas further north than in previous decades.

This year the EU deployed its largest-ever wildfire preparedness operation — 777 firefighters from 14 countries across high-risk areas, backed by 22 aircraft and five helicopters on standby. Yet with fires burning simultaneously in three countries, the limits of even that capacity have been tested.

The EU has also approved funding for a permanent fleet of around a dozen amphibious water bombers, expected from 2027, alongside a new regional firefighting hub in Cyprus. The idea is to shift from reactive scrambling after fires break out toward a standing, coordinated European capability that can act earlier.

Wildfires destroy more than land. The deaths of three firefighters this week — and the thousands displaced in the middle of the night — are a measure of what this season is demanding from communities and the people trying to protect them.
